scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: One check in three places
scenes.caption: Kabir notices that the enquiry screen, review list and response preview each contain a copied version of the exercise rule. One copy has already drifted to a different threshold. Repeating the code has repeated the opportunity for inconsistency.
scenes.dialogue: Can one reliable step serve every caller?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: The copies disagree
scenes.caption: The same record is marked differently depending on which screen checks it. The team needs one shared function with a clear contract rather than three almost-identical sets of conditions. Moving the code must preserve input validation and review paths.
scenes.dialogue: Reuse the check without losing its safeguards.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Describe the contract
scenes.caption: State the function’s input, output and expectations. Use stable IDs, validated scores and explicit document status. A missing field is not automatically zero or false. A shared function must return a visible review result when required information is absent.
scenes.dialogue: An absent value is a real case to handle.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Handle a missing score
scenes.caption: A record has no score value but its documents are complete. Should the shared check silently convert the missing score to zero, mark the record eligible, or return the defined missing-data review route?
scenes.dialogue: Missing is not a numeric score.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Use the same function
scenes.caption: The team runs the same validated function for several records and sees consistent outcomes. Complete and incomplete document flags remain distinct from an unknown flag. The review list and response preview can now share one rule without losing validation.
scenes.dialogue: One correction can reach all the callers.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the logic lab
scenes.caption: Define the contract, check three example calls and test a missing-score case. Explain what the caller receives and when a person must review the record. Syntax is optional; the reasoning must be explicit.
scenes.dialogue: Let us test the shared step at its boundaries.
